case.scope: The control of araC transcription from the Pc promoter in Escherichia coli: the DNA sites in the ara regulatory region, which proteins occupy them (araC protein, CAP with cyclic AMP, RNA polymerase), and what that occupancy does to Pc activity. Induction of the araBAD operon from PBAD belongs to a sibling pathway and is OFF-PATHWAY here. The DNase protection and dimethyl sulfate methylation assays themselves, and any measurement that concerns araBAD expression only, are also off-pathway or excluded.
case.audit: Every quote in this file is verbatim from C:/t/eval-fulltext/PMC319880.r3.txt and from nothing else; r3 is the authoritative text and both earlier revisions were discarded as evidence. Sections read in full: header, abstract, introduction, Materials and Methods, Results (DNA-Protein Contact Sites in the ara Regulatory Region; Polymerase binding sites at PBAD and Pc; The A Site Is a 'Classical' Operator for the araC Gene; The A Site Is Not Within PBAD), Discussion including the four numbered objections to Ogden et al., the abbreviations footnote, the legends of Figs. 1-7, acknowledgements and the reference list (read only to see what is cited). In r3 the body text runs continuously; only a few words remain displaced where lines cross the figure regions of page 3 (for instance the clause reporting that at 250 microM cAMP the CAP protected an additional region at -130 to -140 against DNase digestion, and the 'in the presence of polymerase' lead-in to the same paragraph). Those spans are readable but not quotable word for word, so they are skipped and the affected rows (I9, I10) carry other sentences instead. This is a transcription-control paper: it contains no metabolite conversion, so the content is protein-DNA occupancy (interactions) plus two gene-expression statements. Enzymes with a stated catalytic role: RNA polymerase holoenzyme (purified from E. coli NL20-000; attaches to Pc and protects a 65-bp region from -105 to -170, initiating araC transcription at -148; separately protects -39 to at least +24 at PBAD) - the only catalyst of an on-pathway transformation (R1). Named without a reaction of their own: DNase I and dimethyl sulfate (footprinting and methylation-protection reagents, excluded by SCOPE), the araC protein in its P1, P2 and P1' forms and the cyclic AMP-binding protein CAP (sequence-specific DNA-binding regulators, not catalysts here), and the unnamed 'enzymes required for the metabolism of L-arabinose' encoded by araBAD (a class, off-pathway). No transport step and no compartment appears anywhere in the paper, so the PathBank hint's 'Cytosol' was not carried over. Record-level observations about the hint, not about the paper: PathBank models CAP in pathway 703792 as nucleic_acids id 275, nucleotide_type DNA, although CAP is a protein and PathBank holds the correct protein record (proteins id 10248, cAMP-activated global transcriptional regulator CRP, UniProt P0ACJ8); 'Ara inducer gene' is nucleic_acids id 925, gene_name AraI, DNA; and the pathway uses Activation on six edges against Inhibition on one, so its signs are deliberate claims.

pathbank_alignment.quote: araC gene under autoregulation still produces sufficient araC protein to sustain araBAD activation.
pathbank_alignment.note: araC -> araC protein is stated in one sentence with both sides named (restored whole from r3). Two differences from the PathBank row, recorded rather than resolved: the paper's product is 'araC protein' with no oligomeric state asserted, whereas PathBank types PW_P004116 'Arabinose operon regulatory protein' as a ProteinComplex; and the paper lumps transcription and translation, so the draft row sits in summary_statements. The paper does distinguish P1, P2 and P1' forms of the product, which PathBank does not.

pathbank_alignment.quote: The araC protein binding sites, designated araO and aral, corre- spond, by their locations, to the A and B sites, respectively.
pathbank_alignment.note: araC protein occupies the operator. The quoted sentence is the paper's own identification of araO with its A site, which licenses araO1 = A site; draft I1 carries P2 occupancy and draft I2 P1 occupancy, a distinction PathBank's single araC protein node cannot hold. On the settled ruling that the curator's signs are meaningful, 'activation' on this protein -> operator edge is best read as occupancy switching the operator on; the sign error in this record is not here but at the next edge, PW_I016132.

pathbank_alignment.quote: At Pc, competition between P2 and RNA poly- merase in the induced cell (see Fig. 7A) and between P1 and RNA polymerase in the uninduced cell (see Fig. 7 B and C) maintains the intracellular concentration ofaraC protein at a lowlevel.
pathbank_alignment.note: Contradicted, stated without hedging. The sign is a positive claim, not a sign-free 'acts on': pathway 703792 uses Activation on six edges and Inhibition on one (PW_I016136), so the curator chose between the two signs inside this very pathway. PathBank therefore asserts that the occupied araO1 ACTIVATES the araC promoter, while this paper's central result is that araO/A-site occupancy by either form of araC protein REPRESSES Pc, by competing with RNA polymerase for the same -105 to -147 DNA (draft I3, draft I4), and the quoted sentence states the consequence: araC protein is held at a low intracellular level. The abstract calls araC protein a repressor for araC in both forms, and the Discussion closes on negative control of Pc by P1 and P2.

pathbank_alignment.quote: 4. Our results show that there is no mutual interference in thebindingofaraCproteintotheAsite("araO")andthebind- ingofCAPtothehigh-affinityCAPsite("CRPBAD").
pathbank_alignment.note: PathBank draws araO1 -> CAP. That edge is exactly the Ogden et al. (ref. 12) proposal that araO, when bound to araC protein, prevents the binding of CAP to CRPc or CRPBAD; this paper reproduces that model and then declares it untenable, giving the quoted absence of mutual interference as its fourth reason. Both PathBank references are Schleif reviews, the same lineage as the rejected model. Record-level note: the target of this edge, CAP, is typed in PathBank as nucleic_acids id 275 (DNA) although CAP is a protein and PathBank holds proteins id 10248 / UniProt P0ACJ8. The only CAP exclusion this paper does report is by RNA polymerase at the low-affinity site (draft I10), a different edge.

Left at not_stated; whether it should be contradicted is a product-owner call, so both readings are set out here. Identity is settled: PW_NA000925 is gene_name AraI, so the edge is CAP -> araI. For not_stated: the paper never mentions CAP acting on araI or on the B site in any direction, and silence is not opposition; the whole araI/B-site story is PBAD-side and off-pathway here (draft I15). For contradicted: the paper maps araI to its own B site, puts that site under positive control by P2 at -42 to -80, makes the high-affinity CAP site a separate shared site at -77 to -110, and states that the two interactions are independently necessary for polymerase attachment to PBAD (draft I14) - on that reading a CAP -> araI activation edge misassigns to araI an effect the paper assigns to a different site, and the paper additionally rejects the araI designation for that region.

pathbank_alignment.quote: 1. The start pointforaraC transcription has beenlocated at -148 (9), and to initiate araC transcription, RNA polymerase attachestoPCandprotectsa65-bpregionfrom -105to -170.
pathbank_alignment.note: Pc -> araC, the promoter driving the gene, is stated: Pc is defined as the promoter for the araC gene and araC transcription initiates from it at -148, with the polymerase attaching over -105 to -170. Drafted as reaction R1 rather than as an interaction; draft I5 carries polymerase occupancy of the same promoter. Partial on one point, recorded rather than downgrading the status: PathBank has no transcript entity and no enzyme on this edge, so R1's araC transcript product and its RNA polymerase catalyst have nothing to align to.

Both sides named, same sign, and this is the one Inhibition edge in the pathway, which is what makes the curator's Activation elsewhere a deliberate positive claim. One mechanistic difference worth the human's attention: the paper shows competition for a shared DNA site - the polymerase footprint at Pc is replaced by the araC footprint on addition of P2 - and never claims an araC protein-polymerase contact, which a bare protein -> protein inhibition edge could be read as asserting.

pathbank_alignment.quote: theAresiduesat 114and 137showedreducedmethylation, - - and the region from -105 to the end ofthe fragment at -170 protectedagainstDNase
pathbank_alignment.note: RNA polymerase occupies and acts at Pc: it protects -105 to -170 against DNase I with reduced methylation at the A residues at -114 and -137, attaches over a 65-bp region, and initiates araC transcription at -148. Under the settled sign ruling, Activation here is a positive claim and the paper agrees with it: polymerase occupancy of Pc is what produces araC transcript, and the repression in this pathway works by denying that occupancy.

uncertain.question: araC gene -> araC protein is stated with both sides in one sentence but lumps transcription and translation, so it sits in summary_statements, while PathBank (PW_R1966965) and the pathway's topology treat it as the single reaction. Should the human promote S1 to reactions, and if so keep R1 (DNA -> transcript) alongside it or merge them?

Mostly resolved by r3: a full sentence now names the inhibition of araC mRNA synthesis, and the Fig. 5A legend names the araC transcript. The residue is only that no single sentence names the template, the enzyme and the transcript together.

Product-owner call, left at not_stated. Evidence both ways is set out in that alignment note: silence about CAP acting on araI (not_stated) against the paper's reassignment of PBAD positive control to a separate shared CAP site plus its rejection of the araI designation (contradicted).

PathBank types the product as a ProteinComplex ('Arabinose operon regulatory protein'). The paper names 'araC protein' and asserts no oligomeric state, so a strict entity match would differ even though the chemistry aligns.

The low-affinity CAP site (-130 to -140) lies inside the Pc polymerase attachment site, so I kept I9 and I10 on-pathway, but the paper concludes it is NOT the site of CAP stimulation of Pc. Keep them on-pathway, or exclude them as a rejected mechanism?

L-arabinose and D-fucose change the form of the araC protein, but every consequence the paper measures for those forms is on araBAD except the A-site affinity difference. Keep them on-pathway as ligand-binding interactions, or move them off-pathway?

araO1 = the A site now rests on the paper's own sentence that araO and araI correspond by location to the A and B sites. The residual doubt is only PathBank's name 'araO1', which hints at a two-operator model this paper does not use: it found no araC protein site other than A and B between +26 and -322.

Two observations are stated only in spans where r3 still displaces words: the CAP footprint at 250 microM cAMP over -130 to -140, and the 'in the presence of polymerase' lead-in for I10. Both rows carry other sentences instead; a human with the printed page may want to add the direct quotes.
